No repo skill currently uses git branches (wt-session worktrees use wt/<slug> branches only); a commit in one run sometimes interferes with a parallel run. tl: The parallelism-foundations finding survives validation intact: all 10 KF and 5 N claims are supported at HEAD (b173a4e), with three minor wording sharpenings. Short-lived feature branches are NOT a worthwhile addition for either parallelization goal: worktrees (wt-session.mjs) already are short-lived branches plus tree/index isolation; branches alone isolate nothing that the observed interference needs (the documented cross-run incidents are shared-checkout tree/index interference that only per-worktree isolation fixes), and branch commits in the shared main checkout would re-introduce the exact interferences the worktree protocol removed. Worth including: a run-level lease/owner identity (C1, closes the only unsafe state KF-7/N3, ~50 lines + tests, precedent exists in csm-autoresearch), a pack-bootstrap cross-process lock (C3, 5-10 lines, closes N1, replaces a manual discipline rule), and telemetry partial-tail recovery (C4a, 1-3 lines, closes N2). Defer: progress snapshot compaction (C5) until a run shows pathological growth. Not now: index split (C2), gate/CI scoping (C6), per-emitter shared sequences (C7, moot once C1 lands).
executiveSummary: Pipeline: parallelism-foundations finding (SAVED b173a4e) -> Triage (DEEP/local) -> 5 parallel read-only researchers -> synthesis. Track 1 re-verified every claim of the prior finding against HEAD code: 15/15 supported, no code drift between the 41ae505 pin and HEAD. Track 2 produced the first complete git-usage inventory: only wt-session.mjs creates branches (wt/<slug>); skills commit to current HEAD via git commit --only; nothing pushes except wt-session --push (origin main) and csm-upload (external Pages clone); CI is branch-agnostic (push+pull_request, no filters). Track 3 catalogued 14 interference mechanisms (M1-M14) with historical incidents: 10 are shared-checkout-only and already fixed by per-worktree isolation (unstaged-guard false positives eccbd4c; git add -A sweeps F-011; resets wiping 7 tasks d94f099; hook mid-edit syntax errors in the 2026-08-22 journal; push-my-work branch collision); what REMAINS across worktrees is regenerated whole-tree merge conflicts (payload tree, payload-index.json, capabilities.json - contradicting the AGENTS.md claim that .agents/README.md is the ONLY expected conflict), shared common git config reads, and same-runId concurrency. Track 4 showed feature branches add only ref-level affordances (push/CI/review) over the worktree model, do not isolate working tree or index, and therefore fix none of the tree-level interference while re-introducing it if used in the main checkout. Track 5 costed 7 candidate changes with code sites, tests, gate interactions, and an overlap map to the validated claims. Headline caveats: the interference history is pre-worktree (Aug 2026); live state (4 wt worktrees, one foreign pushed branch, 3 PR merges) shows the mechanism in daily use; no evidence of a remote-collaboration demand driver.

keyFindings.claim: Three wording sharpenings from validation: KF-8 qualifier (checkCompleteness is called in unit tests AND the eval harness, never the run runtime); N4 tail is inference (the two-worktree payload rebase conflict is documented as possible, not test-demonstrated); KF-2 sequence counter is per emitter instance, normally one per process.

Short-lived feature branches are NOT worthwhile for goals 1 or 2 in the current setup: the repo already runs short-lived branches per goal (wt/<slug> via wt-session create/merge/nuke); branches alone provide no working-tree or index isolation (git-worktree semantics), so they fix none of the documented tree-level interference mechanisms (unstaged-guard blocks, git add -A sweeps, whole-repo gate reads, index.lock serialization, reset/clean wipes, in-flight hook edits, shared-checkout branch collisions), and committing to branches inside the shared main checkout would re-introduce the exact interferences the worktree protocol removed.

Branches add only ref-level affordances over worktrees: pushing for remote collaboration, per-branch CI, PR review diffs. Evidence these are real but currently marginal: origin carries three pushed wt/* branches and one foreign branch (pushed manually); ci.yml runs on every branch with no filter; three wt/human-rendering PRs were merged via GitHub. Caveat: wt-session --push pushes origin main only (after ff-only merge), never the wt/<slug> branch, so the PR path required a manual git push origin wt/<slug> that no tooling performs; remote collaboration via PRs would need a small push-branch verb or a documented manual step.

Cross-run commit interference is real but its cause is shared-checkout concurrency, and the fix is per-worktree isolation (already deployed), not branches. Documented incidents (Aug 19-22 2026, pre-worktree): unstaged-guard blocks (eccbd4c --no-verify), the commit-sweep hazard remediated by git commit --only rules (review F-011), concurrent git resets wiping 7 tasks (d94f099), in-flight hook syntax errors blocking commits, duplicate push-my-work branch requiring user intervention, and a sibling approach file whose format-marker mismatch blocked all commits in the checkout. Worktrees fix the shared-checkout mechanisms (M1-M8, M10 same-checkout corruption, M13); what remains across worktrees: M9 regenerated-whole-tree conflicts at merge, M11 shared common-config reads, M12 same-runId concurrency, M10 at merge time. The AGENTS.md claim that .agents/README.md is the ONLY expected merge conflict holds only for non-skill-source runs - skill-source branches also conflict on the regenerated payload tree/payload-index.json/capabilities.json (sound inference from whole-tree byte parity, not test-demonstrated - same hedge as V-2/N4).

WORTH INCLUDING - Run-level lease/owner identity (C1 = KF-7/N3): closes the only genuinely unsafe state. Store surface ~45 lines + driver 10-20 + schema bump; multiprocess store tests exist; the csm-autoresearch ledger is a fail-fast EEXIST-lease precedent (no auto stale-takeover). Benefit is fail-fast detection of same-runId reuse, not new concurrency. Design caveat: durable-json acquireLock/withLock carry open review findings F-033 (stale-takeover can displace a fresh winner -> dual-holder), F-077 (unbounded recursion), F-102 (error masking) at HEAD - the lease should use the ledger-style fail-fast lock or budget a F-033 fix first, not blanket-reuse acquireLock.

WORTH INCLUDING - pack-bootstrap cross-process lock (C3 = N1): ~5-10 lines wrapping packBootstrap in a fail-fast lock (lib/durable-json withLock or EEXIST lock); replaces manual discipline rule A4; closes the module-local packQueue gap; callers unchanged (hosts invoke the CLI, Makefile, tests). Caveats: withLock semantics are fail-fast durable-locked, so concurrent packs become hard errors (a behavior change that enforces A4); the lockfile must live outside the pruned/regenerated payload region and tarball mapping; F-033/F-077 caveat applies if durable-json locks are reused.

WORTH INCLUDING - Telemetry partial-tail recovery (C4a = N2): 1-3 lines in telemetry.mjs list() passing {recoverPartialTail:true,onPartialTail} (or quarantine). The API exists in durable-json; the only production user today is the csm-autoresearch ledger (csm-browse is a beneficiary, not a precedent - its daemon-log prevents partial tails by flush-at-exit and its json-contract reads throw on torn files). Unblocks every post-crash reader of a run telemetry.jsonl. Durable loss records (C4b = N5) are medium effort (~25-45 lines + receipt-schema decision) and worth including as a follow-on: losses currently vanish on exit and the durable receipt drops telemetryLosses.

DEFER - Progress snapshot compaction (C5 = KF-9): the O(snapshots-so-far) rescan is real but bounded per run (single progress cursor per run, runs are finite, evidence dirs are disposable); the fix costs a schema-version bump + both engines + migration + audit-trail care (~30-60 lines + tests). Defer with condition: adopt when a run exceeds ~10^3-10^4 snapshot writes or when resume cost matters; cheapest interim is pruning old snapshots inside the save transaction.

NOT NOW - Index split (C2), full gate/CI scoping (C6), per-emitter shared sequences (C7), trace dead code: the .agents/README.md split costs a ~207-line reorg + gate changes + boilerplate/payload regen for smaller conflict hunks only (conflict stays, same-commit rule stays); C7's shared-sequence hazard exists only in the same-runId scenario that C1 removes, and detectLoss has no production caller. CI note: three wt branches currently sit on origin and ci.yml is unfiltered, so each push fires the full suite including the Docker adapter-integrations job - a minimal ci.yml branch filter (ignore wt/**) is a cheap optional lever worth including if wt-branch pushes continue; the large per-change gate refactor stays out of scope.

WORTH INCLUDING (doc-only) - Correct AGENTS.md:36-39: the 'only expected merge conflict is the .agents/README.md index line' claim holds only for non-skill-source runs; skill-source worktree branches also conflict on regenerated payload tree files, bootstrap/payload-index.json, csm-orchestrate/capabilities.json and generator-owned README regions during rebase. A one-line hedge plus the existing README.md:551 wording already covers it.

detailSections: VALIDATION. Track 1 re-located every citation at HEAD: KF-1 evidence-dir confinement and slug-embedded ids (run-orchestrator.mjs:184-224,331-352; progress.mjs:193,264; skill-executor-handlers.mjs:129); KF-2 writeQueue + append-lock + per-emitter sequence with the judge rewrite confirmed accurate (telemetry.mjs:108-114,161,204; durable-json:129; detectLoss 268-296 vs checkCompleteness receipt-id correlation 249-266); KF-3 canonicalize/digest chain and the 8-field tuple = skill + 7 digests with permissions folded via descriptorDigest (schema-runtime:128-142; capabilities.mjs:51-55; skill-executor-registry.mjs:9-36); KF-4 exclusive atomicWrite plan advancement (plan.mjs:456-462) + sourcePlan.digest binding; KF-5/KF-6 all serializing structures verified (check-suite.mjs:1481-1509,772-813,815-874,708-743; progress records validated untracked 925-945,1511-1515); KF-7 TOCTOU + MonotonicTerminalError + no lease; KF-8 dead trace code + ledger shape + test/eval-only loss APIs; KF-9 both saveProgress (782-786) and loadProgress (830-860) re-read + cursor-index bound; KF-10 lockless writes safe only by run-unique filenames; N1-N5 all supported (module-local packQueue 617-628; partial-tail throw 227-236; DuplicateIdempotencyError 76-81/UNIQUE 284; per-worktree corpus gating; in-memory loss drain index.mjs:161-163 dropped from durable 1614-1633). GIT SURFACE. Sole branch creator wt-session.mjs:102; merge = rebase on origin/main + ff-only in main checkout (140-178); nuke deletes the branch (241-251); prune never touches wt/ (262-314). Hooks: pre-commit only; whole-tree unstaged-guard; whole-repo check-suite; oxfmt restages. hooksPath is shared common config; the shim self-locates per worktree but reads .lefthook.yml from the main checkout (common-dir parent). CI: push+pull_request, no filters. Commits: csm-deep-research default-on at SAVED (commit --only), others only on authorization, csm-orchestrate never commits (checkpoint restore only). INTERFERENCE. M1-M14 catalogue: 10 shared-checkout-only (fixed by worktrees), 4 remaining across worktrees: M9 regenerated-file merge conflicts (payload tree/payload-index/capabilities.json; the AGENTS.md 'only .agents/README.md' claim is false for skill-source runs), M10 pack races (same-checkout corruption + merge conflicts), M11 common-config reads, M12 same-runId concurrency. BRANCHES. Branches add ref affordances only; they neither isolate trees nor indexes; adopting them in the main checkout re-exposes M1-M8/M10/M13; skill commit text needs no changes (all commit to current HEAD); gate timing is unchanged (a per-branch commit gate already exists; payload regen must be committed on each branch; rebase replays without hooks so the merge re-gate stays mandatory). CHANGE COSTING. C1 ~45-70 lines + tests (lease route) or ~10 lines (lockfile route); C3 5-10 lines; C4a 1-3 lines, C4b ~25-45 lines + receipt-schema decision; C5 ~30-60 lines + schema bump + both engines + migration; C2 ~207-line reorg + 2 gate functions + boilerplate/payload regen; C6 trivial filter to large refactor; C7 10-25 lines + interface change + test churn.
recommendation: Decision-ready (findings only - no plan). 1) Feature branches: AVOID as a mechanism for goals 1 and 2. The wt/<slug> worktree flow already provides per-goal short-lived branches with isolation; adopting branches inside the main checkout would re-introduce shared-tree interference; the ref-level increments (push/CI/PR) are already available via wt-session --push and ci.yml with no branch changes. Validation question if revisited: does a second human collaborator need to review or run parallel sessions against the same repo? If yes, the path is the existing wt branches + PRs, still no new machinery. 2) Include now (cheap, closes validated gaps): C1 run lease or .run-lockfile (prefer the lockfile route first; the lease route if DB owner identity is wanted for audits); C3 pack-bootstrap withLock; C4a partial-tail recovery. 3) Include as follow-on (medium): C4b durable loss records - decide the receipt contract first (extend csm-orchestrate-receipt vs sidecar); do not wire detectLoss until loss records are durable. 4) Defer with condition: C5 compaction (trigger: runs exceeding ~10^3-10^4 progress snapshots or measurable resume cost). 5) Do not include now: C2 index split, C6 gate/CI scoping, C7 shared sequences, trace-code wiring. Cost-of-error: C1/C3/C4a are small, low-risk, and each replaces a documented manual discipline rule with a mechanism - rollback is trivial; none changes contracts. What would change these answers: remote-collaboration demand (branches/PRs up), telemetry becoming a product surface (C4b/C7 up), or long-running resume-heavy runs (C5 up).
unverifiedClaims: No claims left unverified. Confidence notes: the N4 tail (payload rebase conflict) rests on inference from byte-parity semantics plus the AGENTS.md/README hedges, not on a planted reproduction; B-2's remote-collaboration increment is evidenced by repo state (pushed branches, 3 PR merges) but demand for it is not measured anywhere; C5 trigger thresholds (~10^3-10^4 snapshots) are judgment calls, not measured.
